usages.explain:
Used to strongly demand from the other party "If I say ..., then you must ...". Comes after the imperative form, the て form.
Often used with the repeated form of the same verb. When used with the imperative form, it's often used by men.

examples.content: 食べろったら食べろよ。
examples.transcription: たべろったらたべろよ。
examples.mean: If you want to eat, eat.

examples.content: 立ってったら立ってよ。
examples.transcription: たってったらたってよ。
examples.mean: If you're standing up, stand up.

title: ったら => speaking of; I told you already; come on (annoyance / dissatisfaction)
